text: The bacterium's cell-wall proteinase cuts casein into a peptide of about 28 amino acids holding both sequences; the cell takes it up and its peptidases trim out VPP and IPP. Falling pH switches the proteinase off, and added amino acids lower the yield.

links.name: Patent EP1581062 (strain, 38-42 °C, times; Evolus = Valio; Calpis sour milk = L. helveticus + S. cerevisiae)

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: The casein is cut into a long peptide by the bacterium, which is taken in and trimmed down to two short ones.

processing.text: Skimmed milk or 9 % reconstituted skim milk powder; preferably 15-50 h. Calpis sour milk also holds Saccharomyces cerevisiae. A run reached pH 4.6 after 9-11 h, was held 5-7 h, then went to pH 4.0.
